defects.prompt: OM651 diesel injector wear / leaks
defects.hint: Only Mercedes OM651 diesels in the 220 CDI (170 hp) and 250 CDI (204 hp) versions of the C-Class (W204), E-Class (W212) and GLK, from the first cars built in 2009. Mercedes stated the 200 CDI, with magnetic injectors, is not affected. The French service measure covered cars built February to August 2009. The same engine in the SLK 250 CDI is treated as possibly affected; the sources do not name that model.

defects.prompt: M271 petrol (pre-2011) balance-shaft/timing gear wear
defects.hint: Only Mercedes four-cylinder petrol engines of the M271 family (1,796 cc), built 2002 to 2015 according to the sources: the supercharged versions and the later turbocharged EVO versions. The sources say cars without the EVO changes are more affected. Mercedes V6 and V8 engines (M272, M273) are not part of this entry.

1.0 EcoBoost coolant/overheating (degas hose, head) — check history
defects.hint: Only Ford 1.0 EcoBoost (Fox) engines built from October 2011 to October 2013. Ford's action covered the Focus; Ford says it also knows of coolant leakage on Fiesta, B-MAX and C-MAX 1.0L engines, so those are listed as likely rather than confirmed in scope.

defects.prompt: 1.0 EcoBoost wet timing belt service due
defects.hint: Only Ford 1.0 EcoBoost (Fox) petrol engines with the oil-bath belts. The US documents cover Fiesta, Focus and EcoSport; the NTN-SNR supplier table also lists B-MAX, C-MAX, Mondeo and Puma with this belt. Parkers says Ford moved to a timing chain in late 2018 and that later Fiesta, Focus and Puma should have a chain, but early ones may still have the belt, so check by VIN or engine code. Recall 23V-905 itself covers only US Focus and EcoSport with the 6F15 automatic.

defects.prompt: Powershift (DPS6) dual-clutch — shudder/jerk on petrol autos
defects.hint: Only Fiesta and Focus with the DPS6 dry dual-clutch automatic. The Ford programmes cover builds from 3 November 2009 (Fiesta) and 1 August 2010 (Focus) to 5 November 2015; the US class action covers model years up to 2016, so the window here runs to the end of 2016. Manual cars are not affected. No document was found for European-market cars: this record is based on US documents only.

defects.prompt: 1.5 dCi injectors + DPF/EGR — clogging, injector wear
Nissan Xtronic CVT — overheating/jerky (check fluid + behaviour)
defects.hint: Only the Nissan Juke (F15) with the Xtronic CVT. The documented programmes are US-only: the warranty extension covers the 2013-2017 model years and bulletin NTB20-091 the 2015-2017 Juke with the RE0F10D (not NISMO RS). The US warranty extension does not apply to EU cars, and no European recall or extension was found. Manual-gearbox Jukes and the 1.5 dCi (manual only) are not concerned. The JF017E chain CVT is not fitted to the Juke.

synthetic.about: Not real vehicles. Exercises generations, fitment tables, every condition leaf and the published-only filter, which the real dictionary does not cover yet.

notes.fillAll: Assemble the checklist for `car`, set every leaf item to `fillAll`, then apply `override` on top.
notes.overallBeforeClamp: The mean of the top-level group scores before the critical clamp is applied. Ports that do not expose it may skip this assertion.
notes.resolveV3: Known-defects v3. Call the port's resolveV3 with `facts` against the bundled canon, or against `v3Fixtures[fixture]` when `fixture` is set, and compare the whole list (order included). Every resolution carries defectId, status, needs, excludedBy and warnings.
notes.resolveDefect: Like resolveV3 for one dossier id; `expect` is null when the id is not a served dossier.
notes.v3Names: resolvedModel(make, model, vin): the dictionary's make id and model id, or null.
notes.v3ServedIds: servedId(id): the served dossier id for a defect id: the id itself when it is a published dossier, the dossier that lists it in `aliases` when it was renamed, else null (deprecated, unknown). resolveDefect itself takes dossier ids only, like the API's reference implementation.
notes.assembleV3: assembleV3(facts): base groups, the fuel module for facts.fuel, then a `defects` group built like /v1/defects in resolve mode: the v2 rule's rows in rule order (id `defect.<v2 id>`, v2 text and critical), each linked to its served dossier via servedId and dropped when that dossier resolves not_applicable, rows without a dossier kept with status `legacy`; then every other dossier on the model that applies or is possible, in id order (id `defect.<dossier id>`, prompt from checklistPrompt, critical from the dossier). The group is titled with the rule's label, or the fixed Known defects title when no rule matched, and is left out when empty. When the make came from the VIN and no rule matched it, the rule is retried with the make's first dictionary name. Compare groupIds, itemCount, defectsTitle (en), the group's ruleId against defectRuleId when the group is there and, per defect row, id, sourceDefectId, dossierId, status, needs, critical, prompt (en) and hint (en, or null).
notes.v3Facts: Facts use the API's names: make, model, year, productionDate (YYYY-MM), fuel, engineCode, engineFamily, gearbox, gearboxCode, cc, powerKw, vin. Ports treat an empty string as absent, trim and upper-case the three codes, and take the make from the VIN's first three characters (vehicles.json makes[].wmi) when no make is given. The VIN is used for nothing else offline.
